newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk preferred shares can be swapped.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk preferred shares can be swapped.

text.p: Holders of preferred shares in Russian mining giant Norilsk Nickel can convert them into more valuable ordinary shares after the sale of a controlling stake in the group goes through on August 5, a spokesman said Friday.

Sergei Vetchinin said the conversion, widely anticipated among Russian share traders, would be consistent with the group's plan to double its authorised capital through issuing 126 million ordinary shares. Shareholders will be asked to vote on the rights issue at an extraordinary meeting on September 8.
"The owner of preferred shares can apply to convert them into ordinaries after the sale of the state stake in Norilsk Nickel," Vetchinin said.
Bids for a 38 percent stake, representing 51 percent of voting shares, close at 4 p.m. local time (1200 GMT) on Friday, with the winner of the investment auction due to be announced on August 5.
Both preferred and ordinary shares in the group have risen sharply during the last few weeks, but the difference between the two has also narrowed on expectations of a share conversion.

At 0845 GMT Friday preferred shares were trading at $13.55 from Thursday's close of $12.90 while ordinaries slipped to $15.20 from $15.30. The shares were trading at $8.30 and $11.75 respectively on July 8.
